artworks.title: Medea
artworks.description: Delacroix's Medea on the threshold of infanticide — the image Euripides made canonical, which the pinned Greek sources only approach in forked traditions: Apollodorus' double account of who killed Mermerus and Pheres, and Pausanias' stoning at the Well of Glauce.

artworks.title: Medea
artworks.description: Leighton's Colchian princess in eastern gold, the witch of Corinth before the robe and the dragon chariot — the eastern sorceress who crossed the sea for Jason and was cast off for a king's daughter.
